newsitem.title: FRANCE: African immigrant elected to French parliament.
newsitem.headline: African immigrant elected to French parliament.

text.p: An immigrant from the West African state of Togo was elected to the French parliament on Sunday to represent a part of the western region of Brittany where there are few immigrants and virtually no blacks.
French television said Kofi Yamgnane, a 51-year-old Socialist, was elected deputy from the Chateaulin area as the country elected a Socialist-led majority to parliament.
Yamgnane, now a French national, first arrived in France in his late teens to study engineering.

He settled in Brittany after marrying a local woman and is mayor of the small village of Saint-Coulitz where he created an African-style "council of wise elders" to help the elected municipal council administer the town.
Yamgnane gained national prominence when appointed junior minister for Integration in 1991, a post he held for two years.

In office, he was widely acclaimed for campaigns aimed at ensuring immigrants were well treated by state administrations. He was less successful when trying to convince Moslems to blend more into French society at large.

Yamgnane is believed to be the first non-white elected to parliament by a mainland France constituency since Gaston Monnerville, the French Guiana-born, longtime Senate president who represented a central France area for decades until the mid-1960s.
Nearly all 22 parliamentarians from French overseas territories are non-white.
